questions.stem: Who was the first President of India?
questions.explanation: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the first President of India (1950–1962) and the longest-serving, holding office for two terms. Dr. S. Radhakrishnan was the first Vice-President (and second President); Dr. Zakir Hussain was the third President and the first Muslim President.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who was the first woman Prime Minister of India?
questions.explanation: Indira Gandhi was the first (and so far only) woman Prime Minister of India (1966–77 and 1980–84). Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman Chief Minister (Uttar Pradesh); Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor (UP) and first Indian woman President of the INC; Pratibha Patil was the first woman President of India (2007).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who was the first Indian to win a Nobel Prize?
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore was the first Indian (and first Asian) to win a Nobel Prize — the 1913 Nobel Prize in Literature for 'Gitanjali'. C.V. Raman was the first Indian to win a Nobel in a science field (Physics, 1930). Mother Teresa won the Peace Prize (1979); Amartya Sen won the Economics Prize (1998).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who was the first Indian woman to go into space?
questions.explanation: Kalpana Chawla was the first Indian-born woman in space (aboard Space Shuttle Columbia, 1997). She died in the Columbia disaster of 2003. Sunita Williams (Indian-American) holds records for spacewalks; Sirisha Bandla flew on a 2021 suborbital flight; Tessy Thomas is the 'Missile Woman of India' (DRDO), not an astronaut.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who was the first Indian to travel to space?
questions.explanation: Rakesh Sharma became the first Indian in space in 1984 aboard the Soviet Soyuz T-11. When PM Indira Gandhi asked how India looked from space, he famously replied 'Saare Jahan Se Achha'. Ravish Malhotra was his backup. Kalpana Chawla was the first Indian-born woman in space (1997).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who was the first Chief Justice of India?
questions.explanation: Justice H.J. Kania was the first Chief Justice of India, serving from 1950 until his death in 1951. B.R. Ambedkar was the first Law Minister and chief architect of the Constitution; M.C. Setalvad was the first Attorney General of India.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which was the first Indian state to be formed on a linguistic basis?
questions.explanation: Andhra Pradesh (then Andhra State) was the first state formed on a linguistic basis, in 1953, carved out for Telugu-speaking people from Madras State — following the death of Potti Sriramulu after a 56-day fast. This triggered the States Reorganisation Act of 1956, which reorganised states on linguistic lines.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who was the first woman to become the President of the Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: Annie Besant became the first woman President of the Indian National Congress in 1917 (Calcutta session). Sarojini Naidu was the first INDIAN woman President of the INC (1925, Kanpur). Nellie Sengupta was the third woman to preside (1933). Besant, an Irish-British theosophist, also founded the Home Rule League.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who was the first Indian to win an individual Olympic gold medal?
questions.explanation: Abhinav Bindra won India's first individual Olympic gold medal in the 10m Air Rifle event at the 2008 Beijing Olympics. Karnam Malleswari was the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal (bronze, weightlifting, 2000); Rajyavardhan Rathore won silver in shooting (2004); Neeraj Chopra later won India's first Olympic gold in athletics (javelin, 2021).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which was the first talkie (sound) film produced in India?
questions.explanation: 'Alam Ara' (1931), directed by Ardeshir Irani, was the first Indian sound (talkie) film. 'Raja Harishchandra' (1913) by Dadasaheb Phalke was the first Indian feature film (silent). 'Kisan Kanya' (1937) was the first indigenously-made colour film. Dadasaheb Phalke is regarded as the 'Father of Indian Cinema'.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who was the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal?
questions.explanation: Karnam Malleswari won India's first Olympic medal by a woman — a bronze in weightlifting (69 kg category) at the 2000 Sydney Olympics. P.T. Usha narrowly missed a medal (4th place) in the 1984 400m hurdles. Mary Kom (boxing, 2012) and Saina Nehwal (badminton, 2012) won bronze later.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who was the first Field Marshal of the Indian Army?
questions.explanation: Sam Manekshaw (Sam Bahadur) was the first Indian Army officer to be promoted to the rank of Field Marshal (1973), following India's victory in the 1971 Indo-Pak war. K.M. Cariappa was the first Indian Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Army (1949) and the second Field Marshal (1986). Only these two have held the five-star rank.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which Indian city was the first to have a Metro Rail system?
questions.explanation: Kolkata Metro, which began operations in 1984, was India's first metro rail system (and is operated by Indian Railways). The Delhi Metro started later in 2002 but became far larger. Kolkata Metro's Esplanade–Bhowanipore (now Netaji Bhavan) stretch was the inaugural section.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who was the first Indian woman to win the Miss World title?
questions.explanation: Reita Faria became the first Indian (and first Asian) woman to win Miss World in 1966. Sushmita Sen won the first Miss Universe title for India in 1994; Aishwarya Rai won Miss World in 1994; Priyanka Chopra won Miss World in 2000. Reita Faria later became a doctor.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which was the first Indian satellite, launched in 1975?
questions.explanation: Aryabhata was India's first satellite, launched on 19 April 1975 from the Soviet Union (Kapustin Yar). Named after the ancient mathematician-astronomer, it was built by ISRO. Rohini (1980) was the first satellite launched by an Indian-made launch vehicle (SLV-3). Bhaskara was an early Earth-observation satellite.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who was the first Indian to receive the Bharat Ratna (in its inaugural year, 1954)?
options: C.V. Raman, S. Radhakrishnan, and C. Rajagopalachari (all three jointly)
questions.explanation: The Bharat Ratna was first awarded in 1954 to three people simultaneously: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan, C. Rajagopalachari, and Dr. C.V. Raman. So there was no single 'first' recipient — all three received it together in the inaugural year. The award is India's highest civilian honour.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which was the first Indian university to be established (among these), in 1857?
questions.explanation: The Universities of Calcutta, Bombay (Mumbai), and Madras were all established in 1857, modelled on the University of London, following Wood's Despatch (1854). Calcutta is often listed first (incorporated 24 January 1857). These were India's first modern universities.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court of India?
questions.explanation: Justice M. Fathima Beevi became the first woman judge of the Supreme Court of India in 1989. Anna Chandy was the first woman judge in India (Kerala High Court, and the first woman High Court judge, 1959); Leila Seth was the first woman Chief Justice of a High Court (Himachal Pradesh).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which Indian was the first to be elected to the British House of Commons?
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji, the 'Grand Old Man of India', was the first Indian (and first Asian) elected to the British House of Commons, winning the Finsbury Central seat for the Liberal Party in 1892. He was also among the founders of the Indian National Congress and authored the 'Drain of Wealth' theory.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which was the first Indian state to implement the Panchayati Raj system (in 1959)?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan was the first state to implement the Panchayati Raj system, inaugurated by PM Nehru on 2 October 1959 in Nagaur district. Andhra Pradesh was the second. This followed the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommendation for a three-tier system. The 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992) later gave Panchayati Raj constitutional status.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who was the first Indian to be appointed as a Judge of the International Court of Justice (ICJ)?
questions.explanation: Sir Benegal Narsing Rau (B.N. Rau) was the first Indian elected to the International Court of Justice (1952), also serving as a judge there. He was the constitutional adviser who prepared the initial draft of the Indian Constitution. Nagendra Singh later became the first Indian President of the ICJ; Dalveer Bhandari is a more recent Indian ICJ judge.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which was the first newspaper published in India?
questions.explanation: 'The Bengal Gazette' (also called 'Hicky's Bengal Gazette' or 'Calcutta General Advertiser'), started by James Augustus Hicky in 1780, was the first newspaper/printed periodical in India. 'Bombay Samachar' (1822) is Asia's oldest continuously published newspaper. 'The Times of India' began in 1838 (as 'The Bombay Times').
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who was the first Indian woman to climb Mount Everest?
questions.explanation: Bachendri Pal became the first Indian woman to summit Mount Everest on 23 May 1984. Santosh Yadav was the first woman to climb Everest twice; Premlata Agarwal was the oldest Indian woman to do so; Arunima Sinha was the first female amputee to summit Everest.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which was the first Indian bank established with entirely Indian capital and management (in 1894)?
questions.explanation: Punjab National Bank (PNB), founded in 1894 in Lahore, was the first bank established purely with Indian capital and Indian management (Lala Lajpat Rai was among its founders). Allahabad Bank (1865) is the oldest joint-stock bank but had British involvement. Awadh Commercial Bank (1881) was the first bank with limited liability managed by Indians, but PNB is credited as the first fully swadeshi bank.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha of independent India?
questions.explanation: Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha (1952–1956); he is often called the 'Father of the Lok Sabha'. He had also been the Speaker of the Constituent Assembly (Legislative). M. Anantha Sayanam Ayyangar was the first Deputy Speaker and the second Speaker.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
